text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Socialists allied with Ecologists and Communists win majority in parliament. Socialist party leader Lionel Jospin expected to be appointed Prime Minister today. Socialists call for an auditing of public finances and a conference on employment. (Les Echos, La Tribune, L'Agefi, Le Figaro, Liberation, IHT).

-- Businessman Francois Pinault questions agreement between state and CDR company selling off Credit Lyonnais assets on buyback by state-controlled entity of a CDR stake in Artemis, the holding that controls retail group Pinault Printemps Redoute.
-- Bouygues SA considers turning into a holding company.
-- Havas media group chairman Pierre Dauzier to name Bertrand Cousin as deputy managing director.
-- OFCE head Jean-Paul Fitoussi says in an interview he sees favourable conditions for economic expansion, calls for a 100-billion franc cut in payroll contributions.
-- Promodes retail group concentrates on most profitable activities, turnover rose 2.9 percent in 1996.
-- Workers at Valeo auto parts maker Evreux plant try to prevent movers to shut down plant.
-- Airbus Industrie to postpone restructuring that would make it an independent company, according to a German newspaper report on Sunday.
